title: Dedicated SLA onboarding decision notebook and prioritization rubric
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Capture a compact, operational decision notebook for enterprise dedicated capacity requests. Purpose: give sales/solutions/CS a deterministic path for SLA targets, reserved throughput sizing, GPU-class recommendation, and burst/scale policies so we can standardize onboarding SLAs and reduce back-and-forth with customers. This artifact combines a triage rubric, example calculations (qps/tokens -> nominal GPUs), a soft-matching GPU class table, and a recommended set of fallbacks for capacity shortfalls. Not a final policy — living document to reduce time-to-proposal and handoffs to ENG and Capacity Operations.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Triage rubric documented with at least 4 SLA bands (platinum/gold/silver/bronze) and corresponding latency and availability targets
A2: Throughput sizing heuristic included (qps, median tokens, peak sustained minutes -> GPU equivalents) with worked examples from 3 anonymized customer profiles
A3: GPU class mapping (A100-80GB, H100, L4, T4-equivalent) with notes on quantization/latency tradeoffs
A4: Burst credit policy drafted (burst windows, credit accrual, preemption rules) and operational playbook for applying burst credits
A5: Hand-off checklist for Eng (config templates, canary rollout steps, monitoring guardrails) and Finance (SLA pricing guidance)
decisions: D1: Use four SLA bands to simplify negotiations — default to Gold unless customer explicitly requests Platinum or constrained to Silver/Bronze
D2: Prefer GPU soft-matching: recommend H100 for latency-sensitive Platinum; A100-80/GPU for Gold; L4-mix for cost-optimized Silver; T4-equivalent for Bronze workloads
D3: Implement a 15-minute burst credit window where customers may exceed reserved throughput up to 2x for short bursts; sustained >15m triggers autoscale evaluation and billing reclassification
D4: All enterprise onboarding must enable token-level tracing and a monitored prompt-set to detect quality regressions during canary
D5: Security review required for any Private/VPC deployment touching regulated data (PII/PHI)
notes: Design: Console needs a one-click 'SLA proposal' export that bundles suggested GPU counts, burst policy, and rollout plan — tracked in ENG-11822
Risk: Over-optimistic burst allowances may starve other pools during peak; propose credit caps per pool and emergency throttles
Pricing: Early estimate shows 18-28% margin compression for Platinum unless we reserve multi-tenant premium pricing or pass-through costs
Edge case: Streaming workloads with 1:1 user sessions require different batching assumptions — call out in worked examples
